subject: Simulated prefetch & batching checks for MAP (tokens/$)
messages:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia@healthgrid.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-24T09:15:00Z
Subject: Simulated prefetch & batching checks for MAP (tokens/$)

Alicia — attaching the first pass of our simulation outputs for the MAP-run: prefetch + batching scenarios. High level summary up front:
- Baseline: 1.0k requests/minute (peak), median request size ~420 tokens, median response ~120 tokens.
- Caching assumption in the baseline sim: 30% prefix reuse (KV cache hits) -> effective tokens served reduced by ~18%.
- Batching behavior observed (under our synthetic trace): average batch size 1.7, p95 batch size 3.
- Effective tokens per $ (hosted profile we used): 21.4k tokens/$ under baseline; with prefetch & cache this improves to ~27.1k tokens/$.

Key caveats: the sim assumes warm workers (no cold-start penalty), and does not include guardrail overhead (audit logging, deep tracing). That increases cost by an estimated +4-6% depending on trace verbosity.

Attached: sim-summary-20261124.csv (overview), batching-prefetch-hypotheses.md (assumptions), cost-breakdown-approx.xlsx (per-scenario tokens/$).

Ask: can you confirm HealthGrid's expected 95th percentile request size (in tokens) and whether the traffic is mostly deterministic prompts (high cacheability) or user-generated free text (low cacheability)? That will materially change the tokens/$ here.

Plan for the MAP: we should lock the evaluation window and run the two additional sims Neha requested (warmup 10m and warmup 30m) against your sample traffic by EOD next Wednesday so we can finalize a unit-econ clause in the pilot SOW.

— Lukas
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sim-summary-20261124.csv (CSV), batching-prefetch-hypotheses.md (text), cost-breakdown-approx.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Alicia Ramos <alicia@healthgrid.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: HealthGrid Procurement <procurement@healthgrid.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T13:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Simulated prefetch & batching checks for MAP (tokens/$)

Thanks, Lukas — good detail. A few quick clarifications from our side: 
- Our peak is typically close to 2.4k req/min for a single region during business hours, but very spiky (bursts up to 4k for short windows).
- Request composition: ~55% deterministic templates (high cacheability), ~45% free-text clinical notes (low cacheability).
- Average request token footprint: user input ~330 tokens, system prompt ~80 tokens, average response target ~150 tokens (so total ~560 tokens per request).

Procurement aside, two questions for your simulations: 
1) Do you capture burst buffering effects? Our infra team is sensitive to p95/p99 latency during short spikes; batching can help but also amplifies tail latency if queueing is aggressive.
2) Is there a way to express the cost estimates as a per-API-call delta (tokens per call -> $ per call) so we can plug into our internal TCO spreadsheets?

If you can provide a short lookup table (call size variants -> $/call) that’d help procurement. Also, we prefer the evaluation window to be 14 calendar days so our security folks can run their scans. Is that compatible with the runs you propose?

— Alicia Ramos
Head of Product, HealthGrid

On the attachments: can you also include the raw trace you used (anonymized) so we can sanity-check the distribution?

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alicia Ramos <alicia@healthgrid.com>
Date: 2026-11-26T08:23:00Z
Subject: Re: Simulated prefetch & batching checks for MAP (tokens/$)

Alicia — quick technical notes and proposed extra sims (I ran a local smoke run last night):
- Burst buffering: our runtime supports a soft-queue and per-worker concurrency cap. In the sim I included both: (a) queue-limited, which reduces p95 but can increase p99 under extreme bursts; (b) scale-to-demand, which reduces tail but adds short-term provisioning cost. I have p50/p95/p99 numbers in sim-summary for both modes.
- $/call table: I converted tokens/$ into per-call cost for 3 representative request sizes (compact, medium, large) using the hosted unit price we used for this pilot. See the small table in the CSV. Example: medium (~560 tokens total) -> $0.000026 per call with 30% caching; with 60% caching that drops to ~$0.000018/call.

Requested extra sims to lock MAP assumptions:
1) HealthGrid traffic profile (your numbers) with cache-hit scenarios at 30%, 45%, 60% (to capture prefix reuse variance).
2) Two warmup regimes: 10m warm pool vs 30m warm pool (this changes effective tokens/$ by ~1.9% in our runs).
3) Burst profile: include 1 simulated 15-minute burst at 4k req/min to produce p99 under each batching policy.

Deliverables: raw anonymized trace (if HealthGrid can provide), the three sim output CSVs, a per-call lookup table, and a short consumer-facing bullet doc we can drop into the MAP for legal/procurement.

Ben — can you run the 60% cache-hit sim and the 4k-burst profile on the hosted stack next business day? If not, note timing and we’ll push to the following day. I’ll prepare the consumer bullets for the MAP and mark acceptance criteria (tokens/$ thresholds, acceptable p99 latency under burst) for the pilot.

— Neha
Principal Applied ML, Redwood Inference

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, HealthGrid Procurement <procurement@healthgrid.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T16:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Simulated prefetch & batching checks for MAP (tokens/$)

Alicia / team — thanks for the quick turn. Finalizing the MAP milestones and dates here so we can lock the SOW and your pilot runway: 
Milestone list (mutual action plan):
- Nov 30: Redwood to deliver three sim outputs (30/45/60% cache-hit) + per-call lookup table + raw anonymized trace request template (DONE/attached).
- Dec 2: HealthGrid to provide anonymized sample trace (or allow Redwood to replay production-like synthetic trace) and sign the pilot SOW with the acceptance criteria.
- Dec 3–16 (14-day evaluation window): Live pilot (region: us-east). Acceptance criteria: median latency under baseline < 120ms, p95 < 360ms during non-burst, and during the 15-minute burst p99 < 1.2s with graceful degradation. Unit-econ gate: tokens/$ must meet or beat the threshold in the lookup table for the agreed cache-hit assumption (we will set conservative assumption = 45% unless you push otherwise).
- Dec 20: Joint readout; operations handoff and procurement checklist complete.

Operational asks for MAP (what we need from HealthGrid):
- Provide anonymized sample trace by Dec 2 (CSV or NDJSON).
- Confirm target SLOs for latency and the preferred cache-hit baseline (30/45/60%).
- Procurement: preferred billing cadence and PO/contract timing (copy procurement on replies).

Ben — if you can confirm compute availability on Dec 1 for the run with 4k burst and 60% cache (rough estimate: 6x NVIDIA A100 equivalence for 15 minutes), we’ll book capacity and drop a short note in the MAP. If compute is constrained we propose a staggered run and will annotate the unit-econ delta.

Alicia — once we have the two confirmations (trace + SLOs) we’ll bake the unit-econ table into section 3.2 of the MAP and call that the gating clause for the pilot close. If anything looks off in the CSVs I attached, flag it and we’ll iterate.

— Lukas
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachments: sim-summary-20261124.csv, batching-prefetch-hypotheses.md, cost-breakdown-approx.xlsx
